records.area: Buffalo Narrows and Peter Pond Lake
records.headline: Special weather statement
records.description:
A significant fall storm continues to affect northern Saskatchewan.

Snow will continue today and into this evening before tapering off overnight, with 5 to 10 cm expected by Sunday morning. In the Pelican Narrows region, rain will change to snow early this afternoon.

Additionally, a period of strong westerly winds, with gusts near 70 km/h, will develop today.

Conditions will improve by Sunday morning.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.

records.headline: Special weather statement
records.description:
Gusty winds are expected.

What:
Westerly winds gusting 70 to 80 km/h.

When:
Late this afternoon through Sunday.

Additional information:
A low pressure system tracking across Hudson Bay will bring strong wind gusts to the region.  Southwesterly winds will gradually strengthen from west to east beginning this afternoon. The winds will then shift to westerly, with the peak winds expected overnight through Sunday morning.  Winds will begin to diminish Sunday afternoon.

Local utility outages are possible. Disruption to services and travel are possible. Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

records.headline: Snowfall warning
records.description:
Snowfall, with total amounts of 10 to 15 cm is expected.

A fall storm will bring significant snowfall along portions of the Coast Mountains. 

Where: Chilcotin (southwestern sections near the Coast Mountains including Tatlayoko Lake).

When: This evening until Sunday afternoon.

Remarks: A strong fall storm will push into the region today with light snow beginning this morning transitioning to snow mixed with rain this afternoon. This evening, the precipitation will change back to snow, and continue into early Sunday afternoon. Areas near Tatlayoko Lake and the Coast Mountains can expect between 10 to 15 cm of snow while the remainder of the region including Puntzi Mountain, will see close to 5 cm.

Travel will likely be challenging. Visibility will likely be reduced at times.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.headline: Wind warning
records.description:
Strong wind gusts expected.

What:
Strong westerly to northwesterly winds gusting up to 100 km/h.

When:
Late this afternoon through Sunday.

Additional information:
A low pressure system tracking across Hudson Bay will bring strong wind gusts to the region. Southwesterly winds will gradually strengthen from west to east beginning this afternoon. The winds will then shift to westerly and northwesterly, with the peak winds expected overnight through Sunday morning.  Winds will begin to diminish Sunday afternoon.

Local utility outages are possible. Some property damage is possible.

If outside, protect yourself from flying or falling debris. Prepare for possible disruptions to transportation, services, and utilities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to ONstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #ONStorm.

records.headline: Wind warning
records.description:
Damaging winds are expected.

What: Northerly winds 70 km/h gusting to 90.

When: Beginning late this evening and easing Sunday morning.

Where: Southern sections of Howe Sound including Bowen Island.

Remarks: The combination of a low tracking southward west of Vancouver Island and a ridge of high pressure over the B.C. interior will create strong outflow winds through Howe Sound. Northerly winds 70 km/h gusting to 90 will develop late this evening over southern sections. The winds will ease on Sunday morning as the low weakens. However, the winds will remain blustery into the afternoon.

Local utility outages are possible. Driving conditions will likely be difficult. There is a risk of injury due to flying or falling debris.

Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to BCstorm@ec.gc.ca or post reports on social media using #BCStorm.

records.headline: Wind warning

Remarks: A vigorous frontal system will impact the B.C. coast and bring very strong southeast winds 90 gusting to 110 km/h to exposed coastal sections of Northern Vancouver Island today. Strong winds will ease below warning criteria this evening as the system moves southward away from the region.

Local utility outages are possible. There is a risk of injury due to flying or falling debris.

Secure loose objects.

records.headline: Winter storm warning
records.description:
A significant fall storm will continue to impact northern Manitoba today and will persist through the weekend.

Where: Areas of northern Manitoba, including, Pukatawagan, Lynn Lake, Brochet, and Tadoule Lake.

What: Hazardous winter conditions including:
Heavy snow with total amounts of 20 to 40 cm.
Severe wind gusts exceeding 90 km/h.
Significantly reduced visibilities in blowing snow.
Freezing rain with total amounts of 5 to 10 mm.
Heavy rain with total amounts of 20 to 30 mm. 

When: Rain and freezing rain developed overnight over northern Manitoba. This will transition to snow throughout the day before tapering off Sunday afternoon. Winds will strengthen throughout the day with gusts up to 90 km/h in areas closer to the Nunavut border and will taper off Sunday afternoon and evening. Visibilities will be drastically reduced in blowing snow this afternoon and evening when falling snow and strong winds combine.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Property damage is possible. Property or tree damage is possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to MBstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #MBStorm.

records.headline: Winter storm warning
records.description:
Hazardous winter conditions are expected due to:
- Snow
- Blowing snow
- Wind

A significant, long duration snowfall event continues with total snowfall accumulations of 30 to 50 cm expected by Sunday morning.

Heavy snow will continue through the day and into tonight before gradually tapering off on Sunday.

In addition to the snowfall, strong northerly winds with gusts up to 70 km/h will continue until Sunday. These winds, combined with falling snow, will result in significantly reduced visibility at times in snow and blowing snow. Winds will gradually ease through the day Sunday.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Local utility outages are likely. Property or tree damage is possible.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.

records.headline: Winter storm warning
records.description:
A significant fall storm will continue to impact northern Manitoba and the Kivalliq today and will persist through the weekend.

Where: Churchill and Arviat

What: Hazardous winter conditions including: 
Snow with total amounts of 10 to 25 cm
Severe wind gusts possibly exceeding 110 km/h.
Significantly reduced visibilities in blowing snow.
Rain with total amounts of 20 to 30 mm.

When: Beginning Saturday morning and tapering off Sunday afternoon.

Remarks: Precipitation will begin in this area today as rain or freezing rain before transitioning to snow and blowing snow this evening and overnight. Very strong winds will occur also, with gusts up to a possibly 100 to 110 km/h, with drastically reduced visibilities in blowing snow. Snow and winds will gradually taper off Sunday afternoon.

Travel will likely be hazardous. Visibility will likely be suddenly reduced to near-zero at times. Local utility outages are likely. High-sided vehicles will be pushed around by the wind.

Prepare for quickly changing and deteriorating travel conditions. Secure loose objects.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to NUstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #NUStorm.

records.headline: Winter storm warning
records.description:
Hazardous winter conditions are expected due to:
- Snow
- Blowing snow
- Wind

A significant, long duration snowfall event continues with total snowfall accumulations of 40 to 60 cm expected by Sunday morning.

Heavy snow will continue through the day and into tonight before gradually tapering off on Sunday.

In addition to the snowfall, strong northerly winds with gusts up to 70 km/h will continue until Sunday. These winds, combined with falling snow, will result in significantly reduced visibility at times in snow and blowing snow. Winds will gradually ease through the day Sunday.

Travel will likely be very hazardous. Road closures are possible. Roofs are at an increased risk of collapse under the weight of snow.

Avoid non-essential travel and outdoor activities.

Please continue to monitor alerts and forecasts issued by Environment Canada. To report severe weather, send an email to SKstorm@ec.gc.ca, call 1-800-239-0484 or post reports on social media using #SKStorm.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 12:48PM MDT until October 24 at 3:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
records.description:

deaths occur in vehicles.

records.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, up to one half foot of
inundation above ground level in low-lying areas near
shorelines and tidal waterways. For the High Surf Advisory,
large breaking waves up to 6 feet in the surf zone. For the
High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal New Hanover County.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 10 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Monday. For the
High Rip Current Risk, until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide.

records.description:

Mexico...

* WHERE...Jemez River above Jemez Pueblo.

* IMPACTS...At 7.0 feet, Between 7 and 8 feet multiple locations
along highway 4 between San Ysidro and Jemez Springs will see water
crossing the road from tributaries and low water crossing points.

could be impacted.

alternative route.

records.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 6:58AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
records.description:
A series of fronts are expected to move across the Interior on
Sunday and Monday. The initial front on Sunday will bring a band
of snowfall across the area. With this first front, light snow
accumulations are expected.

The next front moving across the Interior on Monday will be
accompanied by warmer temperatures, which could bring the
potential for a light rain/snow mix in the valleys and moderate
snow amounts across higher elevations. This could lead to slick
travel conditions, especially during the overnight hours Monday
night into Tuesday when the temperatures could drop below freezing
once again.

Accompanying the second front will be a period of gusty winds
across the higher elevations. This could bring some blowing snow
concerns Monday night/Tuesday morning, which could reduce
visibility to one mile or less.

Stay up to date with the latest forecast by visiting our website,
weather.gov/afg.

records.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 24 at 10:26AM AST until October 26 at 6:00AM AST by NWS San Juan PR
records.description:
* WHAT...Life-threatening rip current.

* WHERE... Across the northern coastal areas including western
and eastern coastal areas.

* WHEN...Remains through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water, where it becomes difficult to
return to safety.
records.instruction:
There is a high risk of rip currents.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as groins, jetties
and piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

If you become caught in a rip current, yell for help. Remain
calm, do not exhaust yourself and stay afloat while waiting for
help. If you have to swim out of a rip current, swim parallel to
shore and back toward the beach when possible. Do not attempt to
swim directly against a rip current as you will tire quickly.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 9:15AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage. The river is forecast to
climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the weekend.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on
or near Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several
inches of water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at
Astor Bridge marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged.
Bartram Rd and Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards
completely submerged. Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded
in South Moon Fish Camp, docks and yards at condominiums on Juno
Trail and water breaches the sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Saturday the stage was 3.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Saturday was 3.2 feet.
- Forecast...A gradual rise is forecast this weekend into early
next week, remaining in Moderate Flood Stage.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
records.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1100 PM EDT.

records.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 24 at 3:36AM AKDT until October 25 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
records.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 4 and 12
inches.

* WHERE...Northern Susitna Valley, including Broad Pass.

* WHEN...From 1 PM this afternoon to 4 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow will develop north of Talkeetna and
across Broad Pass by late this morning or early this afternoon. The
heaviest snow is expected to fall between late this evening and
Sunday morning before tapering off. The snow may mix with rain at
times near the south end of the pass, limiting snow accumulations.
After a break break in the snow, another round of snow is possible
overnight Sunday into early Monday morning.
records.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

records.headline: Flood Warning issued October 24 at 3:38AM MST until October 25 at 12:00AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
records.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...The Little Colorado River from Winslow to Leupp.

* WHEN...Until midnight MST tonight /100 AM MDT Sunday/.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the Little Colorado River is imminent or
occurring. Deadly flooding over low-water crossings.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 333 AM MST /433 AM MDT/, water levels have crested at Winslow
and are expected to fall through the day today. However,
downstream impacts will continue at Birdsprings through at least
this evening.
- For the Little Colorado River at Winslow:
At 3:00am MST /4:00am MDT/ the stage was 18.11 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.0 feet.
Forecast: Water levels are expected forecast to fall below action
stage around 10:00am MST /11:00am MDT/ today.
Impacts:
At 17.0 feet: Downstream, the approaches to the bridge over the
river on Navajo Route 71 near Bird Springs will flood, and Leupp
will be within 3 feet of flooding problems. The river will crest
at Navajo Route 71 approximately 18 hours after the river crests
at Winslow. Minor lowland overflow on right bank at Winslow.
At 18.0 feet: Flow above this level for approximately 6 hours or
more may cause erosion to the levee and eventual leakage or
failure.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Leupp, Birdsprings, Sunrise, Bushman Acres, Homolovi Ruins State
Park and Clear Creek Reservoir.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
records.instruction:
Stay away or be swept away! The banks of rivers are unstable and
unsafe during any flooding event.

Low water crossings will become dangerous. Do not attempt to cross
flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

records.area: San Luis Obispo County Beaches; Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches; Santa Barbara County Southwestern Coast; Santa Barbara County Southeastern Coast; Ventura County Beaches; Malibu Coast; Los Angeles County Beaches
records.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 3:28AM PDT until October 29 at 1:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
records.description:
* WHAT...Minor to moderate coastal flooding expected due to very
high tides.

* WHERE...Coastal areas of Los Angeles, Ventura, Santa Barbara,
and San Luis Obispo Counties.

* WHEN...From 5 AM Sunday to 1 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Minor to moderate flooding of sea water is likely
over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the
time of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike
paths, and harbor walkways. Moderate to significant beach
erosion is likely. Isolated damage of structures due to sea
water inundation is possible to the most vulnerable areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High tides will likely reach 7.5-8.0 feet
(MLLW) each late morning, which is 1.0 to 1.5 feet above
astronomical projections. The highest tides will be Monday
through Wednesday. There is a small chance for isolated Coastal
Flood Warnings Wednesday through Thursday if larger surf
develops.
records.instruction:
Listen to advice from local officials. Do NOT drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth.

records.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued October 24 at 5:15AM EDT until October 24 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, 1 to 2 feet of inundation above
ground level expected in low- lying areas near shorelines and
tidal waterways.

* WHERE...Ocracoke Island.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this evening.
For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until noon EDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Up to 1 to 2 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways
resulting in a low threat of property damage. Some roads and low
lying property including parking lots, parks, lawns, and homes
adjacent to the waterfront will experience shallow flooding. Rip
currents can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into
deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 1 PM today. Tide levels will continue to
rise with King Tide Cycle in place through the upcoming work-
week. The morning high tide will be the highest of the two daily
tides. King Tides peak Tuesday and Wednesday.
records.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

records.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

records.area: Coastal Volusia; Mainland Northern Brevard; Northern Brevard Barrier Islands
records.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 24 at 2:35AM EDT until October 25 at 2:00AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
records.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents. For the
High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 11 feet
expected in the surf zone. For the Coastal Flood Warning,
significant coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Mainland Northern Brevard and
Northern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 2 AM EDT Sunday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Monday evening. For the
High Surf Advisory, from 11 AM this morning to 8 PM EDT
Monday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 2 AM Sunday to 8
PM EDT Monday.

* IMPACTS...Coastal roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Significant shoreline erosion will occur.
Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach
erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
records.instruction:
Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Coastal flooding is occurring or imminent. Coastal residents in
the warned area should be alert for rising water, and take
appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is
required, do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

records.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 12:42AM CDT by NWS New Orleans LA
records.description:
Elevated fire weather conditions can be expected across portions
of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.
Relative humidity values are forecast to drop into the low 20 to
mid 30 percent range. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to
remain at or below 10 mph, which should limit critical fire
weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that
may ignite.

Some improvement in humidity levels is expected on Sunday
afternoon with levels about 10 percent higher (30 to 40 percent)
than this afternoon. An additional 10 percent increase is possible
on Monday, which should lower the threat level somewhat.

Numerous local burn bans are in place and continue to expand across
LA and MS due to ongoing drought conditions. This now includes East
Feliciana, Iberville, Pointe Coupee, St. Helena, St Tammany,
Tangipahoa, Washington and West Feliciana Parishes along with
Wilkinson, Amite, Pike, and Walthall Counties. Regardless, outdoor
burning is strongly not recommended this afternoon, and all local
restrictions followed.

records.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 9:15AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
records.description:
30W was upgraded to Tropical Storm In-fa over the northern Marshall
Islands at 700 AM ChST this morning, located near 10.6N 166.3E, or
120 miles north-northeast of Ujae Atoll, south of Bikini and Rongelap
Atolls. In-fa has maximum sustained winds of 40 mph, which extend
outward 115 miles to the southeast, 105 miles to the southwest, 100
miles to the northwest, and 40 miles to the northeast. This keeps
Ujae Atoll just outside the direct tropical storm-force wind field,
but strong sustained west to southwest winds with damaging tropical
storm-force gusts are expected through at least tonight as In-fa
begins to meander generally northward. The worst impacts will be
felt for islands and atolls across the northern and central Marshall
Islands, especially for west-facing exposures along the Ralik Chain,
such as Ujae, Enewetak, and Kwajalein Atolls. To the south of In-fa,
expect surging west to southwest winds of 20 to 30 knots with gusts
up to 45 knots, especially near heavier showers or outflow
boundaries. Boats should be safely secured away from west or south-
facing exposures, if possible. Significant boat damage has been
reported along west reefs already.

Seas will be hazardous to small craft throughout much of the central
and northern RMI, and dangerous within the tropical storm-force
winds closer to the center of In-fa. Do not attempt inter-island
travel. Even within the relatively calmer lagoon-side waters, inter-
island travel is strongly discouraged. Passing showers may produce
sudden strong to gale-force gusts, which will create locally
dangerous conditions. West to southwest swells will build to the
south of In- fa through the rest of the weekend, leading to elevated,
potentially hazardous surf along west- and south-facing reefs of the
central and northern RMI, mainly to the north and northwest of
Majuro.

Currently, In-fa is nearly-stationary, with its recent motion showing
a slight southeastward drift at around 1 mph, but is forecast to
begin slowly meandering north-northeast, then north-northwest through
this afternoon. Then, In-fa will see a slight increase in forward
speed through Sunday as it begins to exit the Marshall Islands. Winds
and seas will begin to ease through Sunday night, but sea conditions
may remain hazardous to small craft across the northern Marshalls
through Monday night. Light winds and a drier ridging pattern look to
set up across the region by the end of the week. This situation
will be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall
Islands.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGUM.

records.description:

Accumulations of 20-40 mm are expected widely within the warning area through this period, with 60-80 mm possible in some locations, bringing flooding and travel disruption in a few places. Showers will become less frequent later through Sunday afternoon.

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings

records.headline: The strongest winds from Storm Boelo are expected Saturday evening and Sunday morning.
records.description:
Very strong westerly winds associated with Storm Boelo are expected with fairly widespread gusts of 60 to 70 mph and gusts to 80 mph in exposed coastal areas. While strong winds are expected across a wider area with a yellow warning in force, there is higher confidence in impacts and disruption taking place within this amber warning area. The winds will gradually ease from the west during Sunday morning. 

This is an update to the amber warning already in force, as Northern Ireland will see the wind easing earlier than other parts of the UK. 

For further details see https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/weather/warnings-and-advice/uk-warnings
records.instruction:
Driving in these conditions can be dangerous, for yourself and other road users. If you must drive, you can do this more safely by taking the following actions; drive slowly to minimise the impact of wind gusts, be aware of high-sided vehicles/caravans on more exposed roads and be cautious when overtaking, and give cyclists, motorcyclists, lorries, and buses more room than usual.

If you are on the coast, stay safe during stormy weather by being aware of large waves. Even from the shore large breaking waves can sweep you off your feet and out to sea. Take care if walking near cliffs; know your route and keep dogs on a lead. In an emergency, call 999 and ask for the Coastguard.

records.headline: Storm Boelo will bring a very windy and wet spell this weekend with some disruption likely across parts of northern UK. : UPDATED

records.headline: Official WARNING of STORM-FORCE GUSTS
records.description:
There is a risk of storm-force gusts (level 2 of 4).
Max. gusts: 80-100 km/h; Wind direction: south then south-west
records.instruction:
Hazard(s) caused by: single falling trees; objects falling to the ground. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Secure scaffolding and free-standing objects (e.g. screens and platforms/stages). For example, fasten tents and coverings or, if there is enough time, take them down completely. Watch out for falling objects (e.g. large branches, roof tiles) and seek shelter if possible.

records.description:

Height range: > 1000 m; Max. gusts: 65-85 km/h; Wind direction: south then south-west
records.instruction:

Recommendations for what to do: 
Secure free-standing objects (e.g. screens and furniture). For example, fasten tents and coverings. Watch out for falling objects outdoors (e.g. branches).

records.instruction:
Hazard(s) to expect: light objects flying through the air. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Secure loose objects. For example, fasten tents and coverings.

records.headline: Official WARNING of STORM-FORCE GUSTS
records.description:
There is a risk of storm-force gusts (level 2 of 4).
Height range: > 600 m; Max. gusts: 70-90 km/h; Wind direction: south-west
records.instruction:
Hazard(s) caused by: single falling trees; objects falling to the ground. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Secure scaffolding and free-standing objects (e.g. screens and platforms/stages). For example, fasten tents and coverings or, if there is enough time, take them down completely. Watch out for falling objects (e.g. large branches, roof tiles) and seek shelter if possible.

Max. gusts: 55-70 km/h; Wind direction: south then south-west; Increased gusts: in exposed locations ~ 75 km/h
records.instruction:
Hazard(s) caused by: single branches falling; objects flying through the air. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Secure free-standing objects (e.g. screens and furniture). For example, fasten tents and coverings. Watch out for falling objects outdoors (e.g. branches).

records.headline: Official SEVERE WEATHER WARNING of VIOLENT STORM GUSTS
records.description:
There is a risk of violent storm gusts (level 3 of 4).
Height range: > 1000 m; Max. gusts: 90-110 km/h; Wind direction: south-west; Increased gusts: in exposed locations ~ 120 km/h
records.instruction:
Great danger due to: falling trees, high-voltage power lines and scaffolding; falling branches, roof tiles and large objects. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Avoid staying outdoors and seek shelter (e.g. in buildings). Adapt your behaviour in road traffic - be prepared for disruptions to transport routes. If there is enough time: secure or store away outdoor objects. Keep sufficient distance from buildings, trees, scaffolding and high-voltage power lines. Close all doors and windows.

records.headline: Official SEVERE WEATHER WARNING of VIOLENT STORM GUSTS
records.description:
There is a risk of violent storm gusts (level 3 of 4).
Max. gusts: 90-110 km/h; Wind direction: south then south-west; Increased gusts: near showers and in exposed locations ~ 120 km/h
records.instruction:
Great danger due to: falling trees, high-voltage power lines and scaffolding; falling branches, roof tiles and large objects. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Avoid staying outdoors and seek shelter (e.g. in buildings). Adapt your behaviour in road traffic - be prepared for disruptions to transport routes. If there is enough time: secure or store away outdoor objects. Keep sufficient distance from buildings, trees, scaffolding and high-voltage power lines. Close all doors and windows.

records.headline: Official SEVERE WEATHER WARNING of HEAVY PERSISTENT RAIN
records.description:
There is a risk of heavy persistent rain (level 3 of 4).
Height range: > 800 m; Precipitation amounts: 40-60 l/m²; in windward areas: ~ 80 l/m²
records.instruction:
Great danger due to: flooding of roads, subways and buildings near water bodies; possible mudslides. 
Recommendations for what to do: 
Avoid flooded areas and areas at risk. Adapt your behaviour in road traffic - be prepared for disruptions to transport routes. If appropriate, take precautions against flooding. If flooding is expected or has already set in, leave the basement immediately. Keep up to date on the flood situation at www.hochwasserzentralen.de

records.headline: Moderate Wind Related Impact
records.description:
SW-S wind with gusts around 20 m/s (70 km/h).

Possible complications in the energy industry, forestry, and transport. Possible damage to trees and forests. Minor damage to energy infrastructure, property (especially older buildings). Risk of injury from flying or falling objects, especially broken branches. Minor travel delays due to debris and outages.
records.instruction: Secure windows, doors, remove or anchor loosely stored objects, tents, greenhouses, etc. Watch out for falling objects such as branches or roof tiles. When driving, watch out for strong crosswinds at exposed points such as bridges, drive slowly. In the mountains, limit hikes and avoid ridge areas in particular.
records.sourceName: Czech Hydrometeorological Institute (ČHMÚ) via Meteoalarm / EUMETNET

records.description:
In the Ružomberok district winds are expected to rise in some mountain areas
reaching in short blows impact speed of up to 30 - 37 m/s (110 - 135 km/h).
The predicted wind speed is typical for the area and time of the year
it can however pose potential risk for human activities.
records.instruction:
BE AWARE, keep up to date with the latest weather forecast.
Expect some minor disruption to outdoor activities.
